title: 1956 AHSME Problem 34
statement: If \(n\) is any whole number, \(n^2(n^2-1)\) is always divisible by:

solutions.text:
We have \[ n^2(n^2-1)=n^2(n-1)(n+1). \] Among \(n-1,\) \(n,\) and \(n+1,\) one is divisible by \(3.\) If \(n\) is even, \(n^2\) is divisible by \(4;\) if \(n\) is odd, both \(n-1\) and \(n+1\) are even, so their product is divisible by \(4.\) Thus the expression is always divisible by \(12.\) It is not always divisible by \(24,\) since \(n=2\) gives \(12.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Among three consecutive integers there is a multiple of \(3,\) and the factors supply at least two powers of \(2\)
